name: Hatchery

gist.Rubin, the Dragoneer Champion: Whenever she summons a creature by sacrificing another, Rubin may immediately cast a Destruction spell from hand for free. Hard to affect with anything but damage.
gist.Icy Dragonegg: One-health egg, free to summon onto an empty board. If it breaks during her own turn, it freezes any target for a turn.
gist.Flaming Dragonegg: Same egg; breaking on her turn it sets any target on fire for good.
gist.Shimmering Dragonegg: Same egg; breaking on her turn it pays her gold.
gist.Red Dragoneer: Fetches any Drago creature from the deck when summoned; each turn shoots harder for every other Drago creature she controls.
gist.Green Dragoneer: Jumps from hand into the slot of a Drago creature that just died; can sacrifice an older creature for a solid shot at anything.
gist.Black-Thorn Dragon: Needs Drago creatures sacrificed to appear. Heavy shot every turn, and both the dragon and the hero it stands beside ignore all Spells.
gist.Blue-Ice Dragon: Enters by sacrificing two older creatures. Each turn it either freezes a target for two turns or, if the target is already frozen, hits it enormously hard.
gist.Dragolfin: Big dragon whose shot is stronger the more cards remain in her deck.
gist.Sorbereus, the Adapting Dragon: Hits a hero with that hero's own Attack stat.
gist.Luna Pele, the Flame Dancer: Draws a card each time something is set on fire, several times a turn.
gist.Kit, the Shark Researcher: Each Ability she gains fetches a creature or makes you take small hits or discard.
gist.Burning Finger: Cheap single-target burn; Rubin's usual free follow-up.
gist.Victory Phoenix Cannon: Heavy shot that chains into a cheap Destruction spell.
gist.Chosen Sacrifice: Can be sacrificed from hand in place of a creature on the board, and replaces itself.
gist.Deepsea Idol: Cancels a sweep that would hit two or more of her creatures.

plan: Eggs first: free, one-health, and worthless unless they break on Georgie's own turn, when they freeze, burn or pay. She breaks them herself by sacrificing them into Green Dragoneer shots and the Black-Thorn Dragon, and every sacrifice-summon lets Rubin fire a Destruction spell on top. Red Dragoneer finds the pieces, Luna Pele turns burns into cards. Once a Black-Thorn Dragon stands beside a hero, neither can be touched by Spells at all. She plays tight and never wastes a trigger. The weak points are the opening turns, when the eggs can be swept on your turn for nothing, and the fact that her heroes other than the dragon's keeper are ordinary.

looks.early: Two or three one-health eggs and a Red Dragoneer; Georgie arranging them in a neat row.
looks.mid: Eggs cracking on her own turn, a Green Dragoneer in the gap, Rubin casting out of turn order; one of your heroes frozen, another burning.
looks.late: A Black-Thorn Dragon beside Rubin with spells sliding off both, a Dragolfin next door, and exactly the cards she needs in hand.

opening.tell: She has a row of one-health Dragoneggs; they only do anything if they break during her own turn.
opening.why: Swept on your turn the eggs are simply gone, while an early Gathering Storm ticks at the start of HER turn and lets her feed eggs to it for a free freeze and burn.

midgame.tell: A Black-Thorn Dragon has landed beside Rubin: no Spell affects either of them.
midgame.why: Your spells and the Storm do nothing to the dragon or its hero, but Dark Gear, The Yeeting, Snow Cannon and Acid Vial are not Spells; one artifact answers what a whole hand of burn cannot (The Yeeting counts as a kill, so a Green Dragoneer may jump into the gap, but it shields no one).

crisis.tell: Only the hero next to the dragon is spell-proof; Kit and Luna Pele stand in the open, already scorched.
crisis.why: Freeze the dragon for the turn it would kill and put every real spell into the two unshielded heroes; there is no time left to build anything.

endgame.tell: Her last hero stands beside the Black-Thorn Dragon, and your hand is mostly spells.
endgame.why: As long as the dragon is there your spells cannot finish the duel; remove the dragon with The Yeeting or steal it, and the last hero is an ordinary target again.
